title: Germany accuses Russia of orchestrating attempted attack in Leipzig
subhead: For the first time, Berlin has officially blamed Moscow for a 'hybrid attack' after two explosive drones were discovered at Leipzig Airport on August 4. The European Union and NATO have expressed their support for Germany.

France's summer 2026 wildfires lead to unprecedentedly huge carbon emissions
subhead: The EU's Copernicus Earth observation service reported that more than 1.5 million metric tons of carbon were released, a figure not seen since 2003. This comes at a time when France must speed up cutting its greenhouse gas emissions while its forest carbon sink shrinks.

title: US defends Trump's Venezuela oil deal
subhead: Trump met oil executives at the White House on Tuesday as he tries to tame gas prices that are spiraling because of the Iran war, with his administration hoping the Venezuela deal could help. Cheaper oil is a priority for the Trump administration ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November.

title: The dangers of 'eating jet lag': Why eating at irregular hours is bad for your health
subhead: A large-scale French study suggests that men who eat meals at highly variable times between workdays and days off face an increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

title: Venice Film Festival 2026 opens amid controversy
subhead: The 83rd edition of the event has already sparked strong criticism with low American representation, an almost complete absence of female directors in the competition and the selection of the controversial 'DAU' by Russian filmmaker Ilya Khrzhanovsky.

subhead: Hassan will stand trial for 'terrorism glorification' in October, over a tweet citing one of the perpetrators of the 1972 Tel Aviv airport attack. Le Monde looks back at two and a half years of controversies and legal proceedings involving one of France's most prominent pro-Palestinian voices.

title: 'No regulation exists:' Suez Canal becomes gateway for invasive species in the Mediterranean
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (6/6). The opening of a passage between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean led to migrations of 'Lessepsian' species, named after the canal's developer, Ferdinand de Lesseps. Their proliferation, which destabilizes ecosystems, has increased due to overfishing, pollution, coastal building and climate change.

title: 'Even our ancestors do not remember a flood of this scale:' Nepal villagers face apocalypse frozen in mud
subhead: Warned in time, many residents of Devighat managed to evacuate their homes just minutes before the mudslide killed over 900 people in Nepal and China. They have started to return to the village, where rescuers are still looking for survivors and the deceased in extremely perilous conditions.
